== Method ==
  Two independent harnesses, both under $HYAKU_SCRATCH/tsukuroi-r48/R48FalsTmpdirFallback:
  (a) host probe.sh — runs the selftest in background, polls every 50 ms:
      - /tmp/tsukuroi-r3-2-selftest.* (any NEW dir under /tmp),
      - $TMPDIR/tsukuroi-r3-2-selftest.* (fixture present inside the given TMPDIR),
      - /proc/<pid>/cmdline of every live process (reveals the base dir the child
        census processes were actually given).
  (b) namespace probe-ns.sh — `unshare -Urm --propagation private` + `mount -t tmpfs tmpfs /tmp`,
      i.e. a FRESH, PRIVATE /tmp inside the namespace. Any dir seen under that /tmp is
      attributable to this run alone: sibling seats running concurrently on the host
      cannot contaminate the attribution. This is the decisive instrument; the host /tmp
      is shared with ~30 concurrently running sibling seats.
  (c) stray-write audit probe-stray.sh — HOME and CWD snapshotted before/after inside
      the namespace, to catch writes outside TMPDIR entirely.

    OBS-IN-TMPDIR $S/t1/tsukuroi-r3-2-selftest.f8Kk6P; no new /tmp dir attributable.

  namespace-isolated:
    OBS-LEAK-UNDER-TMP /tmp/tsukuroi-r3-2-selftest.LewHLN   (repeats through the run)
    child census root_dir=/tmp/tsukuroi-r3-2-selftest.LewHLN

     the post-fix blob does not. Probe has power; the negative is real.

  Stray-write audit (namespace, HOME+CWD snapshotted):
    "--- NEW paths outside TMPDIR (HOME/CWD//tmp in the private ns): (none)"

== Additional kill-rule probes run (post-fix) ==
  TMPDIR=$S/t missing (spaced, nonexistent):
    fail-fast, no fixture anywhere:
      "selftest: TMPDIR <$S/t missing> cannot host the fixture tree (no /tmp fallback, R48-C2)"
    OBS-LEAK-UNDER-TMP: 0. (No /tmp fallback; the pre-fix blob would have fallen back to /tmp.)
  TMPDIR=$S/missing-clean-dir (clean path, nonexistent):
    mktemp fails loudly, nothing built; no /tmp fixture. (Pre-fix: same, since the path is clean.)
  TMPDIR="" (empty):
    falls back to the mktemp(1) default /tmp — sanctioned by the script's own contract
    (S252: unset or empty means the mktemp default) and by the claim, which lists
    "TMPDIR unset" as an accepted configuration. The kill rule only fires when TMPDIR
    is a WRITABLE NON-/tmp directory, so this is not a kill. Recorded as an observation.
  TMPDIR=$S/tmplink (symlink -> /tmp), namespace-isolated:
    the fixture physically lands in /tmp (OBS-IN-TMPDIR .../tmplink/tsukuroi-r3-2-selftest.nxHgeE
    real=/tmp/tsukuroi-r3-2-selftest.nxHgeE). This is the caller's own TMPDIR resolving

== Risks / caveats ==
  1. The namespace runs report 5 failing selftest cases (161/166). Identical failing set
     for PRE and POST and for every namespace run, and they are exactly the DAC-dependent
     cases (000-permission dir unreadable, unlistable root/record dir). Cause: inside the
     user namespace the mapping makes the 000 fixtures readable, so the "unreadable" arms
     cannot be built. It is an artifact of the isolation instrument, not a defect of the
     script. The HOST runs (no namespace) report PASS (166 cases, 166 passed, 0 failed)
     under both clean and spaced TMPDIR, so the C2 pass condition itself holds.
  2. The post-fix tree under a spaced TMPDIR is reached through a /proc/self/fd/<n>
     alias (fd 240). The physical location is inside TMPDIR (verified by readlink -f),
     but the PATH STRING handed to child census processes is "/proc/self/fd/240/..." —

     the descriptor being inherited by children (works on this host; the R48-C2 selftest
     arms pin both properties). Flagged as a robustness risk, not an observed leak.
